explanation: Patting a child on the head is normal and affectionate, but doing the same to an adult you don't know well can come across as patronizing. Dutch social culture keeps a degree of personal space and formality with people outside close relationships, so unsolicited head-touching outside that circle can feel overly familiar.
local_tip: Stick to a handshake or a brief nod with adults, and save head pats for children or people you know very well.

also_check.note: The head is considered the most sacred part of the body, so touching it — even a child's — is a serious offense.
